pageDescription: Meet RoboGrinder's Infantry, Sentry, Hero, and Engineer robots, designed and built by Virginia Tech students.
headline: Our robots.
intro: From agile ground units to autonomous systems, our robots bring mechanical design, electronics, embedded controls, and computer vision together on the competition field.
imageAlt: Three RoboGrinder competition robots on the arena floor
fleetIntro: Every robot has a role. Explore our 2025-2026 designs and the engineering behind each one.

robots.name: Infantry
robots.description: Infantry robots are agile ground units that lead the offensive line. Equipped with 17 mm projectile launchers, they take on opposing robots in fast-moving encounters.
robots.imageAlt: CAD render of RoboGrinder's 2026 Infantry robot

robots.name: Sentry
robots.description: Sentry is a fully autonomous unit that operates without a human driver. Onboard SLAM, NAV2, LiDAR, and computer-vision tracking work together to navigate the field and engage opposing robots.
robots.imageAlt: CAD render of RoboGrinder's 2026 Sentry robot with its tall sensor mast

robots.name: Hero
robots.description: Hero is a heavy assault unit that combines a high-torque chassis with a launcher for 42 mm, golf-ball-sized projectiles. It is designed to deliver heavy damage to opposing robots and fortifications.
robots.imageAlt: CAD render of RoboGrinder's 2026 Hero robot with its large projectile launcher

robots.name: Engineer
robots.description: Engineer is a non-combat utility unit that supports the fleet with custom grabbing mechanisms that collect resource minerals and revive eliminated teammates. These mechanisms make it the fleet's most mechanically complex robot.
robots.imageAlt: Gray RoboGrinder logo placeholder for the Engineer robot render

ctaDescription: Our robots are built by students working together across five engineering subteams. Meet the people behind the machines or support their next season.
